prompt:
This is a self-contained code experiment. Use only the supplied problem and artifacts. Do not use tools, access files, consult other agents, or search. The evaluator is unavailable. Keep critiques below 250 words. For implementation turns, return only the complete TypeScript source, without Markdown fences or prose.

Review Opus's feedback. Correct errors where justified, preserve valid behavior, and resolve the task. Return the full implementation.

<feedback>
This is the third review of the same code, unchanged since my last round, and I have no new findings. Earlier rounds found two issues: the tokenizer lowercased before splitting, and the single-match branch was hard to read. Both are fixed. I re-checked the code against every spec rule and found no further difference. I recommend that Astra finalize this version instead of convening the council again, because more rounds on identical code will not give new information.

- **Spec coverage I re-checked:**
  - Both selector paths require `type === "select"`.
  - Exact category matches take priority over the token fallback.
  - The fallback skips options with any nonempty category and requires whole ASCII tokens.
  - Missing-selector is returned before the blank-request check, and only the request is trimmed.
  - Groups are flattened one level in encounter order.
  - The four tiers run in order with deduplication by value, ambiguous results do not fall through, and `currentValue` is only compared.
- **Accepted assumption:** `"options" in item` identifies groups. This is safe because the spec says all inputs conform to the types.
- **Not verified:** I could not compile or run the code in this read-only turn. If the harness allows it, a `tsc --strict` pass and some quick checks would be the only useful remaining step:
  - a Kelvin-sign id (U+212A),
  - duplicate values across a group and the top level,
  - an exact-tier match alongside a different case-insensitive match,
  - a blank request with no selector.
</feedback>

checks.name: grouped choices and trimmed case-insensitive request
select type and explicit category take precedence over fallback
mode does not match model substring or another assigned category
fallback aliases use unordered whole tokens and first match
permission policy is a mode fallback alias
exact value outranks earlier exact name
ambiguous exact names do not fall through to a unique weaker tier
duplicate choices with the same value are not ambiguous
case-insensitive matching keeps differently cased values distinct
blank request is a no-op after selector resolution
group name is not a selectable choice
current value is not an implicit choice
choice values and labels retain their own whitespace
